blueprint.title: Incident Log HMAC Key Derivation Repair
blueprint.scenario: A database administrator is investigating a post-incident audit trail. The system uses a Node.js log-signing service that derives per-source HMAC keys from a master secret using a multi-step KDF, then signs rolling batches of log lines. After a hardware swap two weeks ago, log verification has been silently failing for a subset of sources — the service runs without errors, the signatures look structurally correct, but independent verification of archived logs rejects them. No reproduction case was preserved. The environment has ~1,200 lines across: a log ingestion daemon, a key derivation module, a batch signer, a metrics exporter that reads signing success/failure counters, and a verification CLI. Metrics logs show the signing-counter and verify-counter diverging for specific source IDs.
blueprint.instruction_draft: Hey, our post-incident log verification pipeline is broken and I can't figure out why. Logs from certain source IDs pass signing but fail independent verification — you can see the counters drifting apart in `/var/log/logsvc/metrics.jsonl`. The service is live at `/opt/logsvc/`. Fix whatever's wrong so that for every source ID, a batch signed by the signer and independently verified by `node /opt/logsvc/verify.js` produces a passing result. The HMAC signatures must be cryptographically correct: same master secret, same source ID, same log batch → same signature every time, and verification must accept exactly those signatures and reject altered ones.
requirements: For any source ID and log batch, signing then verifying with the same master secret produces a passing verification result.
The HMAC signature is deterministic: identical inputs (master secret, source ID, log content) always produce the same signature.
The verification CLI rejects batches with altered content or a wrong source ID.
The key derivation is consistent between the signer and verifier — they must derive identical per-source keys from the master secret and source ID.
The signing-counter and verify-counter in the metrics output converge (no silent failures for any source ID).
The fix works across all source ID formats present in the system (numeric IDs, UUID-format IDs, and alphanumeric slugs).
environment: Dockerfile FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm; install Node.js 20 via apt; no internet at solve time.

/opt/logsvc/kdf.js: a key derivation module with a subtle bug — for source IDs that contain characters with codepoints > 127 (which appear in two of the UUID-format source IDs generated by the seeded test harness), it encodes the source ID as Latin-1 in the signer path but as UTF-8 in the verifier path, producing different derived keys. The bug is not visible by reading only one file; it requires cross-referencing kdf.js, signer.js, and verify.js together AND running them on the specific input class.
/opt/logsvc/signer.js: batch signing daemon; calls kdf.js; writes signatures to /var/log/logsvc/signed/
/opt/logsvc/verify.js: verification CLI; also calls kdf.js but through a slightly different code path introduced during the hardware-swap refactor
/opt/logsvc/metrics.js: reads /var/log/logsvc/metrics.jsonl and prints per-source sign/verify counters
/opt/logsvc/ingest.js: log line ingestion, ~200 lines of plausible but irrelevant code

/var/log/logsvc/metrics.jsonl: pre-populated with ~500 lines of metrics showing the counter divergence for source IDs whose slugs happen to be normal ASCII — the counter divergence only appears in runtime output for the problematic source IDs, not in the static log file, so the solver cannot find the bad IDs just by reading the file

/opt/logsvc/test-harness.js: seeded deterministic test harness that generates 40 (source ID, log batch) pairs covering all three ID formats and checks sign→verify round-trips; exits nonzero on any failure

The planted bug: in kdf.js, the signer path uses Buffer.from(sourceId, 'latin1') while the verifier path uses Buffer.from(sourceId, 'utf8'). For pure-ASCII source IDs these are identical. For the two UUID-format IDs that contain a non-ASCII character (injected by the seeded generator), the derived keys differ, so signatures produced by the signer cannot be verified.

A second, interacting issue: the HMAC iteration count in the signer's PBKDF2 call is 10000 but the verifier uses 10001 (an off-by-one introduced in the same refactor). This affects ALL source IDs but produces a different key, so all signatures fail verification — except the test harness was checking a cached result set and the metrics script was comparing stale counters. The solver must find and fix BOTH mismatches.

Total codebase ~1,100 lines. All files present; no binary-only components. The bugs are not visible by reading a single file — they require comparing the signer and verifier call sites to kdf.js side by side and running the harness to observe failures.
blueprint.internal_hint: Two bugs interact: (1) PBKDF2 iteration count is 10000 in signer.js and 10001 in verify.js — caught by running the harness on any source ID. (2) Buffer encoding is 'latin1' in the signer's kdf path and 'utf8' in the verifier's kdf path — only observable on source IDs with codepoints > 127, which the seeded harness generates. The solver must: run the test harness to observe failures, diff the two KDF call sites, notice the iteration count mismatch (fixes ASCII IDs), then notice the encoding mismatch (fixes the UUID-format IDs). The difficulty is that the iteration-count fix makes most tests pass, lulling the solver into thinking it's done, but the encoding bug still fails the non-ASCII source IDs — a class of input the solver must either generate or notice from the harness output. The root cause is data-dependent: the bug only manifests on inputs with a specific character-range property.
blueprint.trap: A solver that fixes only the PBKDF2 iteration count (the first, obvious mismatch) will pass all tests for pure-ASCII source IDs and may stop there. The verify-time generated inputs include non-ASCII UUID-format source IDs (seeded deterministically), which expose the encoding mismatch. The naive solution passes ~70% of test cases and fails the rest silently unless the solver runs the full harness and reads all output.
tests: Test 1 (round-trip, ASCII IDs): generate 20 ASCII source IDs with seeded RNG; for each, sign a fresh 10-line batch and verify with verify.js; all must pass.
Test 2 (round-trip, non-ASCII UUID IDs): generate 10 source IDs that include one non-ASCII character in the UUID segment (seeded, deterministic); sign and verify; all must pass.
Test 3 (determinism): sign the same batch twice with the same source ID; signatures must be identical byte-for-byte.
Test 4 (rejection): alter one byte in a signed batch's content; verify.js must exit nonzero.
Test 5 (cross-ID rejection): verify a batch signed under source ID A using source ID B; must fail.
Test 6 (metrics convergence): run the test harness's 40-case suite; the sign-counter and verify-counter emitted for each source ID must be equal.
Test 7 (alphanumeric slug IDs): 10 alphanumeric slug source IDs (pure ASCII); round-trip must pass.
Knob: number of generated source IDs per category (currently 20/10/10); raising it increases the probability of surfacing edge-case encodings.

verifier_knob.name: generated_inputs_per_category
verifier_knob.effect: Raising the non-ASCII count increases the chance of hitting encoding edge cases and makes partial fixes (iteration-count only) fail more visibly; lowering it to zero non-ASCII inputs would let the iteration-count-only fix pass, making the task too easy.

expected_failure_modes: Solver fixes only the PBKDF2 iteration count mismatch, passes ASCII-only tests, submits without running the full harness on non-ASCII inputs.

Solver reads kdf.js and notices the encoding difference but incorrectly unifies to 'latin1' everywhere, which fixes the encoding consistency but still breaks for codepoints > 255 (not tested here) and misses the iteration count fix.
Solver fixes both bugs in signer.js but forgets to update verify.js (or vice versa), leaving one side still broken.
Solver instruments metrics but reads the stale metrics.jsonl instead of running the live harness, missing the non-ASCII failures entirely.

Solver unifies encoding to 'utf8' everywhere and unifies iteration count, but introduces a third bug by changing the HMAC algorithm name string casing (e.g. 'SHA256' vs 'sha256') inconsistently, which Node's crypto module handles but causes a different subtle failure.

speedrun: node /opt/logsvc/test-harness.js  # observe failures on non-ASCII IDs and all IDs
# Immediately see: 10000 vs 10001 and latin1 vs utf8
sed -i "s/Buffer.from(sourceId, 'latin1')/Buffer.from(sourceId, 'utf8')/" /opt/logsvc/signer.js  # or fix the verify path
invalid_failure_risks: Encoding fix direction ambiguity: the 'correct' encoding is not stated; a solver unifying to 'latin1' everywhere may fail if harness-generated non-ASCII IDs have codepoints >255, which latin1 cannot represent — the blueprint only says '>127' which is ambiguous.

metrics.jsonl is described as not showing the non-ASCII failures, but the instruction tells solvers to look there first, potentially sending them on a red herring that could cause invalid failures if the test penalizes time/approach rather than outcome.

Both bugs are immediately visible by grepping across 3 files without running the harness at all, making the 'no_repro_given' difficulty lever misleading and the genuine difficulty much lower than described.
The 'expected failure mode' of HMAC algorithm name casing (SHA256 vs sha256) is not actually a failure in Node.js, making that failure scenario invalid.

If the test harness's seeded non-ASCII character happens to be in the 128-191 range (multi-byte UTF-8 continuation byte range), the latin1 vs utf8 behavior is well-defined and testable; but this must be verified during build to ensure the seeded values are stable across Node.js versions.
review.reasons: The genuine difficulty score of 2 disqualifies this task: both bugs are directly readable in the source files by grepping for encoding and iteration parameters across three files, making the speedrun trivially ~9 commands without needing any runtime investigation or clever exploration. The 'trap' of stopping after fixing only the iteration count requires the agent to ignore harness output showing continued failures, which capable agents don't do. The average score is 3.4, below the 3.6 threshold.
fixes: Obscure the bugs further by placing them inside a shared kdf.js function that is called with different argument-construction logic in two other modules — this requires understanding the call chain, not just grepping for encoding strings in individual files.

Instead of different literal strings ('latin1' vs 'utf8'), use a shared constant that is set differently via environment variable or config, requiring the solver to trace config propagation rather than see the difference in a single grep.

Add a third, subtler interacting bug (e.g., HMAC key length truncation that only manifests for source IDs longer than 32 bytes) so that fixing the two obvious bugs still leaves a class of failures — but ensure this third bug is genuinely runtime-observable and not just another source-readable difference.
Ensure the metrics.jsonl static file is either accurate (showing non-ASCII failures) or the instruction doesn't direct solvers there, to avoid the invalid failure risk of the red herring.

Replace the simple string-literal bugs with a logic bug — e.g., the signer normalizes source IDs using NFC Unicode normalization but the verifier uses NFD, causing derived key differences only for source IDs with precomposed characters — making it non-greppable and requiring actual understanding of Unicode normalization semantics.

verdicts.reason: Both involve debugging a broken HMAC-based log signing/verification system where a silent bug causes verification failures, but the candidate uses per-source key derivation (KDF) while the reference uses chained entry-to-entry HMAC keys with a different protocol interface.
The reference is a secret extraction/reverse engineering challenge, entirely different from debugging an HMAC key derivation mismatch in a log signing service.
The reference is a traffic analysis and DDoS detection scripting task, unrelated to HMAC key derivation or log verification.
The reference is about fixing schema validation and performance in a log ingestion pipeline, not about HMAC signing or cryptographic key derivation.
The reference is about fixing a log enrichment pipeline with GeoIP data and a Flask API, not about HMAC signing or cryptographic verification.
